annotation.title_clean: Revised: Internet-Connected Toys Could Present Privacy and Contact Concerns for Children
annotation.title_en: Revised: Internet-Connected Toys Could Present Privacy and Contact Concerns for Children
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Internet Crime Complaint Center
annotation.summary_en: FBI public service announcement warning consumers about privacy, security and contact risks of smart internet-connected toys with microphones, cameras and GPS. It outlines applicable US law (COPPA, FTC Act) and gives consumer recommendations on encryption, authentication, updates, privacy policies and complaint filing.
key_provisions_or_claims: Smart toys collect voices, images, location and personal data that can be exposed or misused.
COPPA and FTC guidance (June 2017) apply to internet-connected toys and related apps.
Failure to secure toy data may trigger FTC Act Section 5 enforcement.
Consumers should use Bluetooth authentication, encryption, updates, strong passwords and minimal data.
Suspected compromises should be reported to IC3.gov.
